title: Story review
description: The story-doctor's verdict on one concept: does the hook promise something, is the promise paid, does the middle develop, does the ending land, and how many seconds the story actually needs. Written twice per concept — `story/<concept>.json` before anything is built (binding on the video-builder) and `story/<concept>-post.json` on the rendered variants (read by the critic-reviewer). Nobody else writes this file.

level.description: `blocks` is reserved for the three defects that make a video feel cut off: the promise never paid, the close missing, the arc broken. Everything else is `optional`. Marking polish as blocking is how a variant gets re-rendered twice for nothing.

fix.description: One correction, verifiable at a glance: a second, a catalog id, a line. Never an adjective.

what.description: The instruction, concrete enough to apply without asking: which block, which seconds, which id, which line.

why.description: The defect it repairs, in the terms of the arc.

variant.description: Only when the fix belongs to one variant. Left out, it is the concept's and every variant applies it.

use.description: Catalog ids the fix needs. They have to EXIST: asking for a shot nobody has is how a concept ends up padded with the wrong material.

duration.description: The length this story needs, argued in beats. This is the field that stops every video coming out the same length.

declared_s.description: What the concept or the render said.

recommended_s.description: What the story needs. It goes UP when there is more story than time and DOWN when there is padding; never toward a house length.

in_beats.description: The count that defends the number: 'hook 3 + three proofs of 7 + turn 4 + close 3'. A length that cannot be written in beats is a template.

cut.description: Stretches that hold one idea with nothing new.

lengthen.description: Beats that are being starved, with the material that would feed them.

per_variant.description: The seconds each variant needs. A short variant drops development beats and KEEPS the whole arc: it never drops the close.

keeps.description: What this length protects when it is shorter than the concept's.

arc.description: The four questions, each answered with a second and a quote rather than an adjective.

as_the_viewer_would_say_it.description: The promise in the viewer's words: 'it is going to tell me why nobody goes back'. A hook that promises nothing cannot fill this in.

promise_paid_off.description: The single most serious defect there is: unpaid, the video feels cut off however well it is edited.

at_s.description: The second the viewer gets what they were promised, or null when they never do.

largest_gap_s.description: The longest stretch with nothing new and no mini_hook holding the viewer across it.

flat_beats.description: Beats that add what a previous one already added. Three beats saying the same thing are one beat played three times.

kind.description: The mould it uses, or the one it should use.

why.description: Why it lands, or what it stops on instead.

pass.description: `pre` reads the concept before anything is built; `post` watches the rendered variants.

variants.description: The variants this pass looked at. Required in practice on a `post` pass.

verdict.description: `reject` means the payoff is not in the material and no edit will put it there. If the arc is sound, `ship` with one line: a concept that works does not need proof that it was read.

ending.description: Only on a `post` pass: what the last seconds actually do. These are the symptoms verify.py measures on the file (`ending`), read here as story rather than as defects.

still_moving.description: The last frame is mid-pan or mid-gesture. The single thing that reads most as 'it got cut off'.

notes.description: Anything that is not yours — black frames, peaks, quota, language, safe area — goes here in one line and stops there. Two agents fixing the same defect is how a variant gets re-rendered with opposite corrections.
